reason: The cited evidence supports that laser cladding can produce well-bonded coatings on TC4 (E3) and that HEA coatings can improve hardness and wear resistance (E1, E3), but no evidence is provided for the specific Ti-Mo-Nb-W composition, the graded transition layer concept, or the quantitative performance predictions. The key premises about the specific alloy design and its predicted outcomes are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Laser cladding can produce a refractory HEA coating with strong metallurgical bonding and low dilution on TC4
A graded transition layer can minimize thermal expansion mismatch and residual stress at the coating-substrate interface
Refractory element additions (Ti, Mo, Nb, W) induce solid solution strengthening and lattice distortion, increasing hardness
The specific Ti40Mo30Nb20W10 composition forms a fine, homogeneous microstructure with nanoscale precipitates that enhance wear resistance without excessive brittleness
The coating will increase surface hardness by 50-70% and reduce wear rate by 40-60% relative to untreated TC4
